mainTopic: The argument of רבי אלעזר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about a כהן: an ערער, זילותא דבי דינא, or combining single witnesses (רב אשי); then a new land case with a שטר
overview: The גמרא first tests the idea that רבי אלעזר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about how many witnesses make an ערער. It rejects that idea, because רבי יוחנן says everyone agrees an ערער needs two. Instead it builds a case in stages. A man whose father is a presumed כהן is brought down by a rumor and brought back up by one witness. Then two witnesses bring him down again, and one more witness says he is a valid כהן. The first answer says the two sides argue about זילותא דבי דינא, whether a court should avoid reversing itself again. רב אשי objects that this worry would apply even with two witnesses together. So he explains that the argument is really about whether separate single witnesses can be combined. That matches a ברייתא where תנאים, including רבי יהושע בן קרחה and רבי נתן, argue about this. The amud ends by opening a new case: a man on disputed land says he bought it and shows a שטר. The ruling comes on the next amud.

steps.title: An ערער cannot be one witness according to anyone
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs two for an ערער, while רבי אלעזר is satisfied with one, is challenged from רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that an ערער needs two? But רבי יוחנן said that everyone agrees there is no ערער with fewer than two witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the earlier suggestion that the argument is about how many witnesses make an ערער. It then attacks that suggestion with a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone agrees that an ערער needs two witnesses, then רבי אלעזר cannot hold that one witness is enough. So the argument between the two תנאים cannot be about this point. The suggested explanation falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A challenge to someone's status or claim
But didn't he say? (opens a challenge from a known statement)

phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
a challenge requires two;
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין עַרְעָר פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם!
phrases.english: Everyone agrees there is no challenge with fewer than two!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין עַרְעָר פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier suggestion from the daf that the argument is about whether an ערער is one or two witnesses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אלעזר accepts an ערער of one witness and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires two.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן reports that everyone agrees an ערער needs two, so no תנא could hold that one is enough.

steps.title: A new case: a man brought down by a rumor and back up by one witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that an ערער is two. It starts to describe a specific case: a presumed כהן's son is lowered because of a rumor, then raised again by one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, an ערער is two. What case are we dealing with? We hold this man's father to be a כהן. A rumor spread that the son is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה, so we brought him down. Then one witness came and said he is a valid כהן, so we brought him back up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old explanation and starts building a new case. The case has several stages, and this is only the first part of the setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rumor is enough to bring the son down from כהונה. One witness is enough to cancel a rumor and bring him back up. This sets the stage for the next stage of the case, where real witnesses arrive.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier approach for a new one)
With what case are we dealing here? (narrows down the case)
We hold him to have a presumed status (חזקה)
Son of a כהן and a divorcee or a חלוצה; he is a חלל and not a valid כהן
We brought him down / we brought him up (from or to the status of a כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: "Brought down" and "brought up" do not mean moving him physically. They mean taking away or giving back his status as a valid כהן.

phrases.english: Rather, a challenge is two;
and with what case are we dealing here?
For example, where we presume
regarding this man's father that he is a priest;
and a rumor went out about him
that he is the son of a divorcee or the son of a חלוצה,
and we brought him down;
phrases.notes: We took away his status as a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא עֵד אֶחָד וְאָמַר דְּכֹהֵן הוּא,
phrases.english: and one witness came and said that he is a priest,
and we brought him back up;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עַרְעָר תְּרֵי; וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge from רבי יוחנן and sets up a new case to explain the argument.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument is about whether an ערער is one or two witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: An ערער is two according to everyone; the argument comes from a specific multi-stage case.

steps.title: Two witnesses bring him down, then another single witness supports him
steps.stepSummary: The case continues. Two witnesses say he is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה, so he is lowered. Then a second single witness says he is a valid כהן. Everyone agrees the two single witnesses combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then two witnesses came and said he is the son of a divorcee or a חלוצה, so we brought him down. Then one witness came and said he is a כהן. Everyone agrees that the testimony of the two single witnesses joins together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes describing the case and states a point that both sides agree on. This prepares for showing what they actually argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two witnesses against him and two single witnesses for him, who came at different times. Both sides agree those two single witnesses count together as a pair. So the argument cannot be about counting witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimonies combine to count as a pair

phrases.english: Then two witnesses came and said
that he is the son of a divorcee or a חלוצה,
and we brought him down;

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא עֵד אֶחָד וְאָמַר דְּכֹהֵן הוּא.
phrases.english: and one witness came and said that he is a priest.
And according to everyone, the testimony combines,
phrases.notes: The earlier single witness and this new one join to make two for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the case from step 2 and adds a point both sides agree on.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two single witnesses combine according to everyone, so counting witnesses is not the issue.

steps.title: The real argument: honor of the court, as רבי אלעזר sees it
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about worrying for the court's dignity. רבי אלעזר says that once the court brought him down, it does not bring him back up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they argue about worrying for the disgrace of the court. רבי אלעזר holds: since we brought him down, we do not bring him up, because we worry about the disgrace of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the real point of argument. It then gives רבי אלעזר's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going back and forth again and again makes a בית דין look unsure of itself. רבי אלעזר thinks that worry is serious enough to leave the man down, even though there are now two witnesses for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Disgrace of the court; the court looking foolish
The תנא who refuses to bring him back up

phrases.english: And here, about concern for the disgrace of the court
they disagree —
Rabbi Elazar holds:
since we brought him down, we do not bring him up,
we are concerned about the disgrace of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא בְּמֵיחַשׁ לְזִילוּתָא דְבֵי דִינָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting up the case, identifies the real point of argument and gives רבי אלעזר's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the argument to a different reason
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר does not bring him back up because of זילותא דבי דינא.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: no worry about the court's honor
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the court that brought him down can bring him back up. It does not worry about looking foolish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds: we brought him down and we bring him up, and we are not concerned about the disgrace of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the argument. This finishes the new explanation of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the testimony decides the case. Once two witnesses support the man, the court brings him back up, even if that means changing its ruling again.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who brings him back up

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, everyone agrees an ערער needs two witnesses and that the single witnesses combine. רבי אלעזר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue only about זילותא דבי דינא. But רב אשי rejects this explanation in steps 6-7.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a court weighing two things: following the evidence, and protecting its own respect so people take its rulings seriously.

phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
We brought him down, and we bring him up;
and we are not concerned about the disgrace of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר: אֲנַן אַחֲתִינֵּיהּ, וַאֲנַן מַסְּקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אלעזר and completes the explanation of the dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In this answer, the dispute is about זילותא דבי דינא, not about how many witnesses make an ערער. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל brings him back up and is not concerned about it. רב אשי later rejects this answer (steps 6-7).

steps.title: רב אשי asks why the case needs single witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges the idea that the argument is about the court's dignity. If that were the issue, the argument should apply even when two witnesses raise the כהן together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged this: If so, why does the case need one witness at a time? The same argument should apply even with two witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the explanation from Steps 4-5, which said the argument is about the court looking foolish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worry about the court's dignity has nothing to do with how many witnesses raise the כהן back up. Even if two witnesses came together, the court would still be reversing itself. So the special case of two single witnesses would be pointless, and the explanation must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (a strong objection to what was just said)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi challenged it:
If so, why specifically one witness?
Even with two, it would be the same!
phrases.notes: If two witnesses raised him back up together, the court would still be reversing itself. So the dignity worry would still apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אִירְיָא חַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the court-dignity explanation given in Steps 4-5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אלעזר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about worrying for the court's dignity.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The dignity worry does not depend on how many witnesses there are. So setting the case up with single witnesses would serve no purpose.

steps.title: רב אשי says the argument is about combining witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a new explanation. Everyone agrees we do not worry about the court's dignity. The argument is about combining two separate single witnesses, which matches an argument between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Everyone agrees we do not worry about the court looking bad. Here they argue about combining testimony, and they follow the argument of these תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי replaces the earlier explanation with a new one. He also sets up the next step, the ברייתא that shows the earlier argument between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two witnesses who said he is a valid כהן came separately, one at a time. The real question is whether such separate witnesses can be joined into one full pair of עדים. This explains why the case needed single witnesses, which answers רב אשי's own challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The court being made to look foolish or degraded
To combine testimony (join two single witnesses into a full pair)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 3 said everyone agrees the two single witnesses combine. רב אשי is now saying that is exactly what they argue about. This is a brand-new explanation, not a continuation of the old one.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Everyone agrees we are not concerned
about the court looking foolish;
and here, they argue about combining testimony.
And it is the same as the argument of these Tannaim:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא חָיְישִׁינַן לְזִילוּתָא דְבֵי דִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by giving a new basis for the argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the argument is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about the court's dignity, and everyone agreed the single witnesses combine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nobody worries about the court's dignity. The argument is whether separate single witnesses can be combined.

steps.title: The ברייתא about combining witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings three views. The first view says witnesses must see the event together. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says they may see it one after the other but must testify together. רבי נתן says they may even testify on different days.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: Their testimony never combines unless both saw it together. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: even if they saw it one after the other, but their testimony only stands in court if they testify together. רבי נתן says: we hear this one today, and when the other comes tomorrow we hear him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows the argument between תנאים which רב אשי just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן lets the court join witnesses who testify on different days, like the two single witnesses in our case. So רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who raises the כהן back up, follows רבי נתן. רבי אלעזר follows the stricter view that requires the witnesses to come together.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Is established, holds up in court

steps.whatToRemember: Two separate questions: Did they need to SEE it together? Did they need to TESTIFY together? רבי נתן is the most lenient: different days are fine. That is the view רבן שמעון בן גמליאל follows.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
Their testimony never combines,
unless the two of them saw the event together.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
Even if they saw it one after the other.
But their testimony does not stand in court
unless the two of them testify together.
Rabbi Natan says:
We hear this one's words today,
and when the other witness comes tomorrow,
we hear his words.
phrases.notes: So the two testimonies still join, even a day apart. That fits our case, where the two single witnesses came separately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that Step 7 pointed to.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the argument about the כהן matches an older argument between תנאים about combining witnesses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the views of the first תנא, רבי יהושע בן קרחה, and רבי נתן on combining separate witnesses.

steps.title: A new case: a land claim and a sale document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new story. One man asks another what he is doing on his land. The other answers that he bought it from him and has a שטר to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to his fellow: What are you doing on this land? He answered him: I bought it from you, and here is the document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new case about a land argument. This step only sets up the story, and the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was witnesses for a כהן. Now the גמרא turns to an ownership dispute. The man on the land answers with a sale document, a שטר, instead of claiming he has lived there for years.

keyTerms.meaning: A document, here a bill of sale

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his fellow:
What are you doing on this land?
He said to him: I bought it from you,
and here is the document.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְחַבְרֵיהּ: מַאי בָּעֵית בְּהַאי אַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of combining witnesses and opens a new case about a land dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. The step only sets out the case: the man on the land claims he bought it and shows a שטר.
